subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who composed the set work 'Music for a While'?
questions.explain: 'Music for a While' was composed by the English Baroque composer Henry Purcell (1659-1695).

questions.q: 'Music for a While' was written as incidental music for which stage play?
questions.explain: It was composed in 1692 as part of the incidental music for the play 'Oedipus'.

questions.q: What type of repeating bass line underpins 'Music for a While'?
questions.explain: The piece is built over a ground bass (basso ostinato), a short bass pattern repeated throughout.

questions.q: In which musical era was Purcell composing 'Music for a While'?
questions.explain: Purcell was a leading composer of the Baroque period.

questions.q: Who wrote the Queen song 'Killer Queen'?
questions.explain: 'Killer Queen' was written by Queen's lead singer, Freddie Mercury.

questions.q: On which Queen album does 'Killer Queen' appear?
questions.explain: 'Killer Queen' featured on the 1974 album 'Sheer Heart Attack'.

questions.q: In which year was 'Killer Queen' released?
questions.explain: 'Killer Queen' was released in 1974 on the album 'Sheer Heart Attack'.

questions.q: Which member of Queen performs the guitar solo in 'Killer Queen'?
questions.explain: Brian May plays the distinctive multi-tracked guitar solo in 'Killer Queen'.

questions.q: How does the ground bass in 'Music for a While' behave as it repeats?
options: It stays on a single sustained note
It descends in whole tones only
It changes to a new melody each time
questions.explain: The three-bar ground bass rises chromatically, adding tension before returning to its starting pitch.

questions.q: On the word 'drop' (as in the snakes dropping from Alecto's head), how does Purcell set the melody?
options: With repeated falling notes to depict dropping
With a long sustained high note
With silence in the voice part
questions.explain: Purcell uses word painting, setting 'drop' to repeated descending notes to illustrate the meaning.

questions.q: Purcell sets the word 'eternal' to a long run of notes on one syllable. What is this technique called?
questions.explain: Singing many notes to a single syllable, as on 'eternal', is called melisma.

questions.q: What is the main role of the basso continuo in 'Music for a While'?
options: To realise the figured bass with harmony and support the voice
To double the vocal melody exactly throughout
To provide a percussive drum pattern
To play a contrasting solo above the voice
questions.explain: The continuo (e.g. harpsichord and bass instrument) fills in harmony from the figured bass to accompany the singer.

questions.q: Queen create their thick, layered vocal harmonies in 'Killer Queen' mainly through which studio technique?
options: Recording all voices live in one take
Using a synthesiser to imitate voices
questions.explain: The dense backing vocals are built up by overdubbing multiple vocal layers using multi-track recording.

questions.q: The close-harmony backing vocals in 'Killer Queen', moving together in the same rhythm, create which texture?
questions.explain: Voices moving together in the same rhythm to harmonise a tune produce a homophonic texture.

questions.q: What does 'syllabic' word setting mean?
options: One note sung to each syllable
Many notes sung to one syllable
questions.explain: Syllabic setting gives each syllable a single note, making the text clear.

questions.q: Which term describes a texture where a single melody has no accompaniment?
questions.explain: A monophonic texture consists of a single unaccompanied melodic line.

questions.q: A singer holds a long, sustained note on the word 'eas'd' in 'Music for a While'. This is an example of what?
options: Word painting depicting relief from pain
questions.explain: The long, calm note on 'eas'd' paints the meaning of being eased of pain, an example of word painting.

questions.q: A vocal line sings twelve notes to the single syllable 'love'. How would you describe this setting?
questions.explain: Many notes sung to one syllable is described as melismatic setting.

questions.q: In the studio, a Queen backing part is sung, then recorded again and again and stacked on top of itself. Which technique is being used?
questions.explain: Recording additional layers on top of an existing track is called overdubbing, key to Queen's layered vocal sound.

questions.q: You hear a tune in the top voice supported by chords that all move in the same rhythm beneath it. Which texture is this?
questions.explain: A clear melody with chordal accompaniment moving in the same rhythm is a homophonic texture.
